To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the azimuthal asymmetry in the J / ψ suppression can be used to determine the onset density of QGP and the survival probability of J / ψ in non-central heavy ion collisions.

the azimuthal asymmetry is a sensitive probe of the initial state effects and that the initial state effects are the dominant source of the observed J / ψ suppression at low p T in the NA50 experiment.
the azimuthal asymmetry coefficient v 2 is proportional to the survival probability S and that the ratio v 2 / S is independent of the centrality and the energy of the collision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the azimuthal asymmetric suppression of J / ψ in non-central heavy ion collisions.
the azimuthal asymmetry in the suppression of J / ψ in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC energies.
the azimuthal asymmetric effect in the J / ψ suppression at SPS and RHIC energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NA50 data are consistent with the onset of suppression at a critical energy density of 1 GeV/fm 3, but the data do not allow us to draw a conclusion whether or not this onset is caused by the QGP effect.
the azimuthal asymmetry is a powerful tool to study the J / ψ suppression mechanism in non-central heavy ion collisions.
if there is a QGP effect, it must be present in both the NA50 data and the RHIC experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
if the J / ψ suppression at the NA50 is caused by a QGP medium, it must be azimuthally asymmetric.
the azimuthal asymmetry is an important observable for studying the J / ψ suppression mechanism in non-central heavy ion collisions. [1]
the NA50 data on J / ψ suppression at SPS energies are not sufficient to conclude that the QGP is created in these collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the azimuthal asymmetry can be used to distinguish the initial state nuclear effects from the final state effects in J / ψ production in heavy-ion collisions.   1.
the azimuthal asymmetric effect is an important observable to study J / ψ suppression at the RHIC.
the azimuthal asymmetry is a very sensitive probe of the QGP effect on J / ψ suppression and thus can be used as a signature for the QGP effect.
